tasks.short: Produce HR reports showing hiring, onboarding, retention, absence and workforce costs across our three sites.

today.trigger: A scheduled management report or a request from HR, Finance or a site manager.
steps: Check the nightly AFAS extract and retrieve recruitment or training data needed for the report.
Reconcile employee counts, dates and site assignments across the sources.
Calculate agreed measures in Power BI or Excel.
Investigate unusual movements and write an explanation.
Check access and distribute the report to its intended audience.
drudgery: Explaining the same metric definitions repeatedly
today.time_sinks: Custom cuts by site, shift and contract type; inconsistent definitions; checking whether apparent movements are data errors.

lenses.faster: Scheduled data loads and reusable measures replace exports, spreadsheet calculations and formatting. AI drafts commentary from validated aggregates, with links to the figures behind each claim.
lenses.autonomous: After a successful refresh, standard reports run and reach approved audiences automatically. Failed checks stop distribution and create an exception for me.
lenses.ambitious: Follow every hiring cohort through day 90 by site, role and recruitment channel. Show productive retained hires alongside time to hire so faster recruitment does not hide poor outcomes.
lenses.joy: Remove copying and formatting. Keep the conversations about why a cohort struggled and what managers can change.
lenses.options: Generate alternative views by site, shift, channel and employment type using the same definitions. Compare operational and executive presentations without rebuilding calculations.
lenses.altitude: I own the reporting definitions, checks and distribution rules. I spend more time testing whether the reports lead to useful decisions.
reach: Prepare recurring workforce reporting for HR Business Partners
Supply reconciled workforce cost inputs to FP&A
Prepare aggregate evidence for works council discussions

tasks.human_edge: Agreeing what productive means for different jobs, interpreting operational causes and deciding which findings deserve management attention.
tasks.pattern_why: Standard calculations and publication rules are checkable and should run without a model. An optional llm_step can draft commentary, but its claims must match approved figures.

in_practice.trigger: A successful nightly refresh or a scheduled reporting deadline.
steps: Load available AFAS, Recruitee and Studytube data through approved interfaces.
Check freshness, join coverage, totals and cohort eligibility before calculating measures.
Generate standard reports from approved definitions and suppress small groups under the agreed disclosure policy.
Draft commentary using only validated aggregates and flag unexplained changes.
Distribute approved standard reports and send novel requests or failed checks to the analyst.
in_practice.human_gate: Approve definitions, audiences and templates before activation; review novel reports and substantive AI commentary before publication.
data_needed: Stable employee and hire identifiers
Vacancy, offer, start and exit dates
Agreed productivity milestones and day-90 cohort rules
Site, role, shift and employment type
Approved absence and workforce cost definitions
Audience permissions and disclosure thresholds
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint reporting register recording refresh time, checks, definition version, recipients and approvals.

evidence.claim: Power BI supports scheduled refresh, reusable measures and report subscriptions.
The proposed savings are planning estimates; Noordhaven's integrations and review workload have not been measured.

risks: Productivity or retention definitions can distort the North Star, especially when recent hires have not reached day 90.
Small site or shift groups can reveal personal information even in aggregate reports.
AI commentary can imply causes that the data does not establish.
Nightly data cannot support claims about live staffing.
research_questions: How many reporting hours go to exports and formatting versus interpretation and approval?
Can recruitment records be reliably linked to AFAS hires and agreed productivity milestones?
Which reports can use preapproved templates, and which require review every time?
What access and small-group disclosure rules have HR and the privacy owner agreed?

tasks.short: Get reliable HR information to the right managers on time and tell them when data is delayed.

today.trigger: A reporting deadline, dashboard refresh, information request or complaint about missing information.
steps: Check whether the relevant extracts and dashboards refreshed.
Identify the intended audience and confirm their access.
Send reports, links and explanations through Outlook or Teams.
Chase missing inputs and respond to access problems.
Correct outdated copies or clarify conflicting figures.
today.time_sinks: Access changes, refresh failures and managers using old attachments instead of the current report.

lenses.faster: Refresh checks, subscriptions and maintained audience groups replace daily checking and repeat emails. Reports display their data date and a single current link.
lenses.autonomous: Successful refreshes trigger distribution; failures trigger a delay notice and an assigned incident. Missing submissions generate reminders according to agreed deadlines.
lenses.ambitious: Give each site a predictable HR information service with explicit freshness and response targets. Track whether managers receive and use information in time to act.
lenses.joy: Remove chasing and link forwarding. Keep direct help when a manager needs to understand a decision or an unexpected result.
lenses.options: Offer a dashboard, a short scheduled digest or an exception alert according to the manager's needs. Test which delivery method results in useful action.
lenses.altitude: I design the information service and monitor its reliability. I manage delivery rules and exceptions instead of acting as the distribution list.
reach: Maintain HR reporting audience groups with IT approval
Coordinate recurring site management information packs
Manage reporting service targets for HR and Finance

tasks.human_edge: Choosing what warrants interruption, understanding a manager's information needs and resolving competing priorities during incidents.
tasks.pattern_why: Freshness checks, audience routing, reminders and escalation rules are explicit. A model is unnecessary for routine delivery.

in_practice.trigger: A refresh result, reporting schedule or overdue input.
steps: Check refresh completion and source timestamps against agreed service targets.
Resolve recipients from approved groups and verify report permissions.
Send subscriptions or current report links when checks pass.
Send a delay notice and create an incident when freshness checks fail.
Escalate unresolved incidents and report delivery performance to the analyst.
in_practice.human_gate: Approve new audiences, sensitive delivery routes and escalation rules; IT or the designated access owner approves permission changes.
data_needed: Report owners and approved audience groups
Refresh status and source timestamps
Delivery schedules and service targets
Incident owners and escalation rules
Input submission deadlines
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint delivery and incident register with timestamps, recipient groups, failure reasons and resolution owners.

evidence.claim: Power BI supports subscriptions and row-level security for controlled reporting audiences.
Power Automate supports scheduled workflows and notifications through Microsoft 365 connectors.

risks: Recipient groups can become outdated after transfers or departures.
Automated attachments can spread sensitive data beyond dashboard access controls.
Too many alerts can cause managers to ignore important exceptions.
A successful refresh can still contain incomplete source data.
research_questions: Which refresh and delivery events are available under the current Power BI licences?
Who owns audience groups, access approvals and incident escalation?
How often do current delays arise from extraction failures versus missing source entries?
Which notifications do managers actually use?

tasks.short: Keep our HR data pipelines, Power BI dashboards and metric definitions working as systems and CAOs change.

today.trigger: A refresh failure, source-system change, new reporting requirement or revised CAO rule.
steps: Inspect errors, source changes and affected reports.
Update queries, mappings, measures or dashboard layouts.
Reconcile results against source records and agreed examples.
Check permissions and downstream dependencies.
Publish the change and update documentation.
drudgery: Tracing broken column names and mappings
Finding downstream reports affected by a change
today.time_sinks: Poorly documented dependencies, source changes discovered after failure and checking measures against changing employment rules.

lenses.faster: A coding assistant drafts query fixes, DAX changes and documentation from a clear brief. Automated regression checks identify broken totals and permissions before release.
lenses.autonomous: Scheduled monitoring detects schema changes, failed refreshes and unusual data movements. It creates a proposed fix and test results without deploying the change.
lenses.ambitious: Build reliable checks for every important HR metric and maintain a record of its source and owner. Catch changes before managers see misleading figures.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive fault tracing and manual comparison. Keep system design and solving the difficult exceptions.
lenses.options: Compare a small repair, a model redesign and a replacement integration. Evaluate maintenance effort, licence cost and reporting disruption.
lenses.altitude: I set the architecture and release standards for HR information. I review changes and improve reliability instead of repeatedly repairing the same failures.
reach: Coordinate HR source-system changes with IT
Own shared workforce metric definitions used by Finance
Set acceptance checks for supplier integration changes

tasks.human_edge: Understanding business meaning, deciding how CAO changes affect measures and approving changes that influence payroll, access or management decisions.
tasks.pattern_why: Maintenance requires diagnosis across tools and often changes business logic. AI can propose and test changes, but the analyst must approve production releases.

in_practice.trigger: A monitoring failure, detected source change or approved maintenance request.
steps: Collect error logs, dependency information and a sanitised sample of the affected data.
Draft a minimal repair and explain which measures or reports it changes.
Run checks in a test environment against approved reference cases.
Present the change, test results, access impact and rollback steps for approval.
Deploy the approved version and monitor the next refresh.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves every production change; payroll, access and CAO-related changes also require the relevant business or IT owner.
data_needed: Current queries, measures and model definitions
Source schemas and dependency records
Sanitised test data and expected results
Approved CAO interpretations
Access rules and rollback versions
in_practice.logs_to: The development repository and a restricted SharePoint change register containing approvals, test results and deployed versions.

evidence.claim: GitHub Copilot provides coding assistance and can help draft code changes and explanations.
Automated regression checks can compare workforce totals and metric outputs with approved reference cases.

risks: A technically valid change can silently alter the meaning of an HR metric.
Production personal data could be exposed through coding prompts or logs.
Source interfaces or current licences may limit testing and deployment automation.
An incorrect CAO interpretation can propagate into cost forecasts or payroll-related reporting.
research_questions: Are there separate development and production environments with reliable rollback?
Which recurring failures consume most maintenance time?
Are metric definitions and dependencies documented well enough to test changes?
Can the approved coding environment operate with synthetic or minimised data?

tasks.short: Help HR and site managers fix access problems, understand figures and use our dashboards.

today.trigger: A user sends a question or reports a problem through Teams or Outlook.
steps: Ask which report, filter, period and result caused the problem.
Reproduce the issue and check data freshness and permissions.
Determine whether it is a usage question, definition issue or technical fault.
Explain the answer, fix the fault or refer it to the responsible owner.
Record useful guidance for repeat questions.
drudgery: Answering repeat filter and definition questions
Searching old conversations for previous solutions
Redirecting requests to the correct owner
today.time_sinks: Vague questions, intermittent faults and requests that mix technical support with disputes about the underlying HR process.

lenses.faster: A structured support form collects report details upfront. An assistant searches approved guidance and drafts a sourced answer or diagnostic checklist.
lenses.autonomous: Routine navigation and freshness questions receive approved answers automatically. Permission requests, conflicting figures and unresolved faults go to the appropriate person.
lenses.ambitious: Make support accessible to managers on all three sites and across shifts. Use recurring questions to improve dashboard design and guidance.
lenses.joy: Remove repeated explanations and missing-detail exchanges. Keep coaching users and solving problems that need judgment.
lenses.options: Offer a short answer, illustrated instructions or a brief coaching session. Compare likely fault causes before changing a report.
lenses.altitude: I manage a support knowledge base and improve the products generating the questions. I review unresolved cases and answer quality.
reach: Provide first-line guidance for HR reporting tools
Create dashboard training with Learning and Development
Supply recurring usability issues to IT and report owners

tasks.human_edge: Recognising when a dashboard question masks a management concern, explaining sensitive findings and taking responsibility for a correct resolution.
tasks.pattern_why: Support mixes repeat questions with ambiguous technical and business problems. AI can gather details and draft answers while the analyst leads substantive diagnosis.

in_practice.trigger: A support request submitted through an approved Teams or SharePoint entry point.
steps: Collect the report link, filter settings, data date and a description without unnecessary employee details.
Search approved guidance within the requester's existing permissions.
Draft an answer with source links, or propose diagnostic steps when guidance is insufficient.
Have the analyst review substantive answers and route access or source-data changes to their owners.
Record the resolution and propose knowledge-base updates for approval.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst reviews substantive replies and fixes; designated owners approve access and source-record changes.
data_needed: Approved metric definitions and user guidance
Report ownership and escalation routes
Refresh status
Requester's report permissions
Sanitised past resolutions
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint support register with the request, cited guidance, reviewer, resolution and any approved knowledge update.

evidence.claim: Microsoft Copilot Studio supports agents that use configured knowledge sources.
Savings depend on the share of repeat questions and the quality of Noordhaven's support guidance.

risks: An assistant can provide a confident answer based on outdated definitions.
Retrieval must respect the user's permissions rather than the analyst's broader access.
Support messages and screenshots can contain employee personal data.
Automatically closing requests can hide unresolved issues.
research_questions: What proportion of requests are repeated navigation or definition questions?
Is the guidance current, owned and searchable?
Can the assistant enforce requester-level access to every source?
Does a pilot reduce resolution time without increasing incorrect answers or reopened requests?

tasks.short: Track which internal teams need HR analytics and where existing reports are underused.

today.trigger: A reporting review, new stakeholder request or recurring gap in HR information.
steps: Review report usage and requests from HR, Finance and site managers.
Identify teams with unanswered workforce questions or little use of available reports.
Discuss their needs and the decisions they need to make.
Prioritise reporting improvements and support.
Check whether the delivered information is useful.
drudgery: Combining usage figures and request lists
today.time_sinks: Discovering needs that never become formal requests and distinguishing useful reporting from dashboard activity alone.

lenses.faster: Combine usage summaries, requests and service feedback into one stakeholder view. AI groups written requests into suggested themes for review.
lenses.autonomous: A monthly workflow flags unmet requests, declining report use and stakeholder groups without suitable information. It prepares a review queue without contacting people automatically.
lenses.ambitious: Give every site and HR value stream a defined information owner and a reviewed set of decision needs. Track whether analytics helps managers act, alongside adoption.
lenses.joy: Remove manual request sorting. Keep listening to managers and finding overlooked questions worth answering.
lenses.options: Compare a new report, improvements to an existing report, training or stopping an unused report. Estimate effort and likely benefit for each.
lenses.altitude: I manage the HR analytics service portfolio. I decide which needs deserve investment instead of accepting every dashboard request.
reach: Maintain the HR analytics demand backlog
Support HR Business Partners with stakeholder needs analysis
Coordinate adoption reviews with Learning and Development

tasks.human_edge: Understanding needs that usage data cannot reveal and agreeing priorities without treating managers as scores.
tasks.pattern_why: For this HR role, customers are interpreted as internal analytics users, not logistics clients or job candidates. Software combines usage and request data; an LLM proposes themes from text, which the analyst checks.

in_practice.trigger: A monthly service review or a new batch of analytics requests.
steps: Collect permitted report usage summaries, open requests and submitted service feedback.
Apply fixed rules to identify overdue requests and gaps in stakeholder coverage.
Extract suggested themes from request text with links to the original requests.
Present reporting, training and retirement options for analyst review.
Update the approved backlog and track whether completed changes help the intended users.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves themes, priorities and stakeholder outreach; usage measures cannot become individual performance assessments.
data_needed: Agreed internal stakeholder groups
Report inventory and available usage metrics
Submitted requests and service feedback
Existing backlog and estimated effort
Approved purpose and retention rules for usage information
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint analytics service register linking suggested themes to evidence and recording approved priorities.

evidence.claim: Power BI provides usage metrics for reports.
Interpreting this O*NET task as internal HR analytics demand is a contextual assumption requiring confirmation.

risks: The original task may refer to external customers and may not belong in this HR role.
Report usage is a weak proxy for usefulness and can unfairly favour office staff over shift managers.
Individual usage monitoring may require works council involvement and an AVG/GDPR assessment.
Automated themes can overlook urgent needs expressed by only one stakeholder.
research_questions: Does this task mean internal analytics users, or is external customer analysis actually part of the role?
What usage information is available and permitted for this purpose?
Can service value be measured through decisions or manager feedback rather than clicks?
Would this review identify needs that the current HR Business Partner process misses?

tasks.short: Build HR dashboards, data models and spreadsheets that answer workforce questions reliably.

today.trigger: An approved reporting need that existing tools cannot answer.
steps: Clarify the decision, users and required measures.
Inspect sources, identifiers and available data interfaces.
Design the data model and build queries, measures and outputs.
Test calculations, access and usability with representative users.
Publish the tool and document ownership and maintenance.
today.time_sinks: Unclear requirements, unavailable interfaces, unreliable joins and revisions after users see the first version.

lenses.faster: AI drafts queries, measures, test cases and dashboard layouts from an agreed specification. Reusable data models reduce repeated integration work.
lenses.autonomous: An approved request can trigger a draft build in a test environment. Publication waits for calculation, privacy and user acceptance checks.
lenses.ambitious: Build a complete vacancy-to-day-90 view connecting recruitment, onboarding, training and retention. Add explicit productivity milestones agreed with operations.
lenses.joy: Remove boilerplate and repeated formatting. Keep designing useful tools and watching managers discover an answer they could not see before.
lenses.options: Produce several working prototypes with different levels of detail. Compare usability, maintainability and source-data requirements before choosing.
lenses.altitude: I become the product owner and architect for HR analytics tools. I define acceptance criteria and approve reusable components.
reach: Prototype onboarding completion tools with HR Administration
Build certificate coverage views with Learning and Development
Create workforce planning inputs with FP&A

tasks.human_edge: Choosing the right problem, designing fair and useful measures and accepting responsibility for the tool's business meaning and access controls.
tasks.pattern_why: AI can produce much of a specified build, but requirements, source interpretation and release approval remain consequential human work. The earlier automate label does not justify unattended publication.

in_practice.trigger: An approved brief with named users, measures and acceptance criteria.
steps: Confirm the brief, source permissions, metric definitions and integration feasibility.
Generate a draft model, queries and output using synthetic or approved minimised data.
Run calculation, join, freshness and access checks against reference cases.
Review prototypes with the analyst and representative site users.
Publish the approved version with an owner, refresh schedule and rollback procedure.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves architecture and release; HR or Finance owners approve definitions, and relevant privacy and OR requirements are resolved before activation.
data_needed: Approved user needs and acceptance criteria
Source schemas and available interface permissions
Stable identifiers and join rules
Synthetic or minimised test data
Metric definitions, access rules and reference results
in_practice.logs_to: The development repository and a restricted SharePoint product register with specifications, tests, approvals and released versions.

evidence.claim: GitHub Copilot provides assistance with generating and modifying code.
Power BI supports data models, calculated measures and interactive reports.
A complete cross-system day-90 tool at Noordhaven is a proposed implementation, not a documented case.

risks: A plausible prototype can conceal incorrect joins or double-counted workers.
Agency portals may lack usable interfaces or stable worker identifiers.
Training completion cannot be assumed to prove productivity.
Tools used for recruitment selection, employee evaluation or consequential work allocation need assessment under the EU AI Act and applicable employment rules before use.
research_questions: Which approved source interfaces and licences are actually available?
Can the analyst define reference results before AI starts building?
Which requested tools involve individual employment decisions rather than aggregate reporting?
Do users accept generated prototypes faster without increasing post-release defects?

tasks.short: Keep personnel reporting records consistent and compile reliable figures on hires, transfers, appraisals and absence.

today.trigger: A personnel change, reporting deadline or inconsistency found in the AFAS extract.
steps: Retrieve personnel changes and relevant absence or appraisal status fields.
Check missing dates, duplicate records, site mappings and employment categories.
Ask HR Administration or Payroll to resolve source-record discrepancies.
Compile agreed personnel statistics and reconcile totals.
Record corrections and publish the permitted summaries.
today.time_sinks: Effective-date inconsistencies, agency workers mixed with employees and different denominators used for absence and turnover.

lenses.faster: Fixed validation rules identify missing or conflicting fields as data arrives. Approved statistical definitions replace repeated spreadsheet calculations.
lenses.autonomous: The nightly extract triggers validation, reconciliation and standard summaries. Source-record exceptions are assigned to authorised owners.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain a dated record of workforce movements and data quality across all sites. Distinguish employees and agency workers so workforce comparisons remain meaningful.
lenses.joy: Remove row-by-row checking and repeated correction emails. Keep resolving meaningful exceptions and helping owners improve source data.
lenses.options: Show headcount, FTE and worked-hours views with explicit denominators. Compare absence and turnover across suitable periods without changing the definitions silently.
lenses.altitude: I own personnel data quality and statistical definitions. HR Administration maintains source records while I monitor the controls.
reach: Coordinate personnel data quality with HR Administration
Provide reconciled workforce movement inputs to Payroll
Prepare aggregate absence reporting for HR Business Partners

tasks.human_edge: Resolving ambiguous employment histories, agreeing denominators and protecting employees from misleading or unnecessarily detailed reporting.
tasks.pattern_why: Record checks, effective-date rules and statistical calculations can be specified and verified. Unclear source facts require an authorised person rather than an AI guess.

in_practice.trigger: A successful nightly AFAS extract and any approved agency-data import.
steps: Load only fields needed for approved personnel reporting.
Apply effective-date, completeness, duplication and workforce-category checks.
Reconcile headcount and FTE movements and calculate agreed statistics.
Route source discrepancies to HR Administration or Payroll without changing uncertain records automatically.
Publish approved aggregates and retain a traceable record of exceptions and corrections.
in_practice.human_gate: Authorised source owners approve record corrections; the analyst approves new definitions and sensitive reporting cuts.
data_needed: Employee identifiers and effective-dated employment records
Hire, transfer and exit dates
Contract hours, site and employment category
Approved absence duration fields and denominators
Appraisal completion status where required
Agency worker identifiers and permitted reporting fields
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint data-quality register, with source correction references retained in AFAS where supported.

evidence.claim: Power Query supports repeatable data transformations and joins for reporting.
Rule-based checks can validate personnel dates, completeness and reconciliation totals.

risks: Absence data is sensitive; reporting must exclude diagnoses and unnecessary medical details.
Absence statistics do not fulfil Wet verbetering poortwachter case-management obligations.
Incorrect effective dates can misstate retention, transfers and workforce costs.
Employee and flex-worker statistics can become misleading if their coverage and denominators differ.
Appraisal content is more sensitive than completion status and requires a separate justified purpose.
research_questions: Which personnel fields generate the most corrections, and who owns each field?
Are headcount, FTE, turnover and absence denominators agreed across HR and Finance?
Can historical effective dates be retrieved reliably rather than reconstructed from current records?
Can the reporting purpose be met with absence duration and appraisal completion status alone?

tasks.short: Track regional labour-market trends that affect hiring, pay and staffing in Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.

today.trigger: A workforce planning review, persistent vacancy difficulty or a request about regional hiring conditions.
steps: Collect published labour-market information and relevant CAO developments.
Compare trends for logistics roles and the three site regions.
Combine external findings with internal hiring, pay and retention figures.
Check source dates, definitions and conflicting evidence.
Write a briefing with implications and options for HR and operations.
today.time_sinks: Different geographic boundaries, lagging publications, occupational categories that do not match Noordhaven's jobs and uncertain causal interpretation.

lenses.faster: Scheduled retrieval and extraction replace repeated source searches. AI drafts a cited briefing while fixed calculations handle comparable indicators.
lenses.autonomous: New publications or agreed threshold changes trigger a draft regional update. The analyst reviews source quality and implications before distribution.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain an evidence-based labour-market view for each site and critical job family. Test recruitment and workforce plans against several plausible market conditions.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive searching and table copying. Keep connecting external evidence to practical hiring and staffing choices.
lenses.options: Compare recruitment channel changes, training routes, pay options within the applicable CAO and different flex-worker mixes. Show assumptions and uncertainty rather than one confident forecast.
lenses.altitude: I design the labour-market monitoring and scenario process. I judge evidence and help HR distinguish a local process problem from market pressure.
reach: Supply sourcing insights to Recruiters
Support regional pay analysis with Compensation and Benefits
Provide workforce assumptions to FP&A and site planning

tasks.human_edge: Assessing source relevance, challenging causal claims and interpreting local conditions that aggregate publications cannot capture.
tasks.pattern_why: Research requires several retrieval, extraction and comparison steps, with variable source quality. The draft is checkable, but strategic conclusions need analyst approval.

in_practice.trigger: A new publication from an approved source or a scheduled regional review.
steps: Retrieve approved publications and record publisher, publication date, reference period and source location.
Extract relevant regional and occupational indicators, flagging uncertain table readings.
Calculate comparable trends and identify mismatched definitions or missing periods.
Combine findings with validated internal aggregates and draft cited implications and scenarios.
Submit the briefing for analyst review before adding it to the management information pack.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst verifies material claims and approves publication; HR leadership and relevant specialists decide pay, staffing or recruitment actions.
systems: An approved document extraction and language-model service
data_needed: Approved source list and permitted retrieval methods
Regional and occupational mappings
Publication dates, reference periods and definitions
Internal vacancy, offer acceptance and retention aggregates
Applicable CAO constraints and approved planning assumptions
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint evidence register with source copies or references, extracted indicators, calculation versions and briefing approvals.

evidence.claim: CBS StatLine provides published statistical tables that can support repeatable external-data analysis.
UWV publishes labour-market information relevant to regional workforce analysis.
An automated, cited regional briefing for Noordhaven is a proposed workflow rather than a documented implementation.

risks: Published regional or occupational categories may poorly represent Noordhaven's recruitment catchment.
Publication lag can make a current-looking briefing describe old conditions.
Extraction errors or invented citations can undermine strategic decisions.
Regional correlations cannot establish why Noordhaven's offers are rejected.
Market analysis does not replace specialist interpretation of applicable CAO provisions.
research_questions: Which sources offer sufficiently current data for the actual recruitment catchment of each site?
Can Noordhaven's job families be mapped to external occupational categories without misleading comparisons?
Which external indicators have historically helped explain internal hiring outcomes?
Does an automated pilot produce verifiable briefings with less review effort than manual research?

role.altitude: The role becomes the owner of Noordhaven's HR information products, data controls and decision evidence, with routine production handled by tested software.
reach: Own cross-system measurement of vacancy-to-productive-and-retained-at-day-90 outcomes
Coordinate personnel data quality with HR Administration and Payroll
Provide workforce cost and capacity inputs to FP&A
Support Recruiters with regional labour-market and recruitment-channel analysis
Support Learning and Development with onboarding and certificate coverage reporting
Prepare controlled aggregate information for HR leadership and works council discussions
role.ceiling_note: These eight tasks cover 894.5 of the implied 1,600 annual role hours, about 56%. Applying the estimated human-time reductions suggests roughly 534 hours of gross capacity, worth about EUR 41,600 at EUR 78/hour; this is a planning estimate, not a cash saving. Integration work, licences, maintenance and review consume part of that capacity, and shared workflows must not be counted twice. The remaining role work is unassessed. The analyst cannot absorb medical judgments, payroll accountability, CAO interpretation or consequential employment decisions simply because reports become cheaper.
skills_to_grow: Power BI modelling, DAX and reliable data integration
Version control, meaningful automated checks and safe releases
Metric design for productivity, retention and comparable cohorts
AVG/GDPR data minimisation, access design and retention controls
Working with the OR on personnel-data systems and monitoring arrangements
Assessing EU AI Act requirements before employment-related AI uses
Source verification, scenario analysis and distinguishing correlation from causation
Product ownership and clear communication with shift-based operations
role.ambitious_version: Run a trusted HR evidence service across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo. Connect vacancies, hires, onboarding, certificates, agreed productivity milestones and day-90 retention; surface data-quality failures before publication; and give HR and operations tested options for improving hiring outcomes. Begin with standard reports, delivery and personnel checks, then reinvest verified capacity in better definitions, regional scenarios and evaluating changes. Use deterministic software for numbers and routing, approved AI for bounded drafts, and accountable people for employment decisions.
